schema.title: agent

query.description: Optional model spec followed by the prompt. Model is one of 'claude', 'codex', 'gemini-code' (defaults), or a full spec like 'claude/opus'; omit it when `agent` / `resume` / `continue_last` provides one. The prompt may instead be passed via `prompt_flag` or `prompt_file`.

prompt_flag.description: The instruction, as a flag instead of the positional PROMPT. Give it one way or the other, never both.

prompt_file.description: Read the instruction from a file; '-' reads stdin, which is heredoc-friendly. The file is read once at spawn, so editing it afterwards cannot change the run.

agent.description: Load agent profile by name. Resolves .lionagi/agents/<NAME>/<NAME>.md first, then .lionagi/agents/<NAME>.md, then a trusted+enabled plugin's declared profile ('<plugin>/<NAME>', or a bare NAME when only one plugin declares it). Profile provides system prompt, default model, effort, yolo, timeout, resume_on_timeout. CLI flags override profile settings.

list_profiles.description: Print every agent profile `agent` would resolve, as JSON, and exit without running anything. Use it to find out what names are available here.

resume.description: Continue a previous run by its branch id, keeping that conversation's history. Cannot be combined with `context_from`, which is for starting fresh.

continue_last.description: Continue the most recently used branch, keeping its history, without having to look up its id.

preset.description: Apply a built-in agent configuration preset. Supported values: coding. 'coding' wires CodingToolkit with path-guard hooks and a coding system prompt; cwd defaults to the invocation directory.

form.description: Path to a YAML or JSON work-form spec file. The spec declares typed fields and values; validation runs BEFORE any LLM call. Exits rc=1 on validation error. Validated values are injected into the prompt as structured context.

image.description: Attach an image file to the prompt (repeatable, e.g. --image a.png --image b.jpg). Supported extensions: .gif, .jpeg, .jpg, .png, .webp. Each file is read, base64-encoded, and attached as an image content part on the user message.

context_from.description: Inject distilled context from a prior session id, branch id, run id, or file path into this new branch's first instruction, above the prompt. Repeatable (concatenated in argv order); the total budget (see `context_budget`) is shared across all refs. Rejected in combination with `resume` or `continue_last`.

context_budget.description: Total token budget for `context_from` content (default 8000; ~4 chars/token).

mcp_config.description: Read this MCP config and hand its servers to the leg explicitly. By default the nearest .mcp.json at or above the directory this command was run in is used, so the leg's tools come from the submission rather than from `cwd`. The file is read once at spawn.

no_mcp_config.description: Hand the leg no MCP servers, and say so deliberately instead of arriving there by an empty search.

yolo.description: Auto-approve the agent's tool calls, so an unattended run is never left waiting.

bypass.description: Bypass all codex approvals and sandbox (for cloud/codespace environments).

fast.description: Route codex requests through OpenAI's priority service tier (lower latency; requires account eligibility). Does not change model or reasoning effort.

verbose.description: Stream the agent's output as it is produced instead of printing only the final result, and silence the progress lines that would interleave with it.

theme.description: Pick the colour scheme printed output is tuned for: 'light' or 'dark' terminal.

effort.description: Override effort (overrides spec suffix). claude: low|medium|high|xhigh|max. codex: none|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max|ultra (max/ultra clamp per model support). gemini-code/gemini-cli: folded into --model as Low|Medium|High (Gemini 3.1 Pro has no Medium).

cwd.description: Directory the agent's process runs in — the repo or worktree it acts on. Defaults to the current directory.

timeout.description: Hard wall-clock timeout in seconds. When set, a [DEADLINE] preamble is injected into the agent's prompt so the agent knows its time budget and can pace reasoning accordingly.

invocation.description: Parent invocation id (from `li invoke start`). Groups this session under a skill orchestration record. Optional.

project.description: Explicit project name for this session. Overrides auto-detection from .lionagi/config.toml or git remote.

resume_on_timeout.description: If the run terminates on `timeout`, automatically fire one resume of the same session with 'continue and conclude the task' and report the combined result. Bounded to a single auto-resume; a timeout on the resumed leg terminates normally. Same effect as an agent profile's 'resume_on_timeout: once'.

notify.description: Shell command template run once this run reaches its terminal status. Overrides .lionagi/settings.yaml notify.on_terminal. Substitutes {payload} (full JSON), {status}, {invocation_id}.

schema.description: Spawn a single subagent and wait for its final response. Flags may appear anywhere relative to the positionals. Use `resume` / `continue_last` to continue a previous conversation. Use `agent` to load a profile from .lionagi/agents/. Use `preset` to apply a built-in agent configuration. Use `form` to load and validate structured inputs before invoking. Use `context_from` to hand a new agent distilled context from a prior session/branch/run/file.

name.description: Role or mode to print in full, including its prompt body. Looked up in both catalogs, so you need not know which it is. Omit it to list names only.

modes.description: List the behavior overlays (modes) instead of the personas (roles). Only affects the bare listing; ignored when a name is given.

id.description: Id of the dispatch to acknowledge, as listed by `li dispatch ls`.

token.description: The ack_token this dispatch was delivered with, reported by `li dispatch show`. A mismatched token is refused, so an acknowledgement cannot be guessed.

status.description: Show only rows in this status: pending, delivering, delivered, acked, dead_letter or expired. Omit to list every status.

limit.description: Maximum rows to print, newest first (default 50).

schema.title: dispatch purge

id.description: Id of a single dispatch to delete, whatever its status. Omit it to bulk-delete by `status` / `before` instead; one of the two is then required.

status.description: Bulk purge: match this status exactly, including pending/delivering (explicit status is deliberate operator intent).

before.description: Bulk purge: match rows with updated_at <= this epoch-seconds value. Without `status`, this is scoped to terminal statuses only (delivered/acked/dead_letter/expired) and never sweeps pending/delivering rows.

dry_run.description: Report what would be deleted without deleting (single-row and bulk).

schema.description: With ID: delete that one row (any status), auditable via admin_events action=dispatch_purge. Without ID: bulk-delete by `status` / `before` (at least one required, so a bare `purge` cannot mass-delete); `dry_run` reports counts without deleting. An explicit `status` is honored exactly as given, including pending/delivering (naming an in-flight status is deliberate operator intent). A bare `before` with no `status` is scoped to terminal statuses only (delivered/acked/dead_letter/expired) and never touches pending/delivering rows.

id.description: Id of the dispatch to re-queue for delivery.
Id of the dispatch row to show, as listed by `li dispatch ls`.

schema.title: doctor

json.description: Emit a JSON object of check name -> {status, detail} instead of plain text.

schema.description: Environment preflight: install location + editability, Python/venv, the import chain `li --version` traverses, core dependency importability, Studio daemon reachability, and ~/.lionagi writability.

schema.title: engine run

kind.description: Engine kind to run. One of: coding, hypothesis, planning, research, review.

spec.description: Main input for the engine (topic / artifact / spec / findings / prompt).

test_cmd.description: Test command to validate generated code (required for 'coding' kind). May be a shell string or a quoted list.

export_dir.description: Directory to save engine outputs to (optional; supported by 'coding' and 'hypothesis' kinds).

dedup_repo.description: GitHub repo to check findings against before extraction ('hypothesis' kind only). Findings whose mechanism an existing open or closed issue already covers are recorded and not expanded; certified-new findings land in the export's filing queue. The engine never files issues itself.

dedup_cwd.description: Checkout of the dedup repo so the novelty check can source-confirm a finding's cite ('hypothesis' kind only; optional).

model.description: Model to use (provider/name, e.g. claude/sonnet; an effort suffix like codex/gpt-5.6-luna-high is honored). Overrides per-stage defaults. Uses engine defaults if omitted.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for all stages (e.g. low, medium, high, xhigh). Overrides per-stage defaults; a per-stage default applies otherwise.

max_depth.description: Maximum recursion/expansion depth for the engine (kind-specific default).

max_agents.description: Maximum number of sub-agents the engine may spawn.

session_id.description: Associate this engine run with an existing session in StateDB (written to engine_runs.session_id).

invocation_id.description: Parent Studio invocation id. Defaults to LIONAGI_INVOCATION_ID; an explicit value takes precedence.

no_persist.description: Skip writing the engine run record to StateDB.

schema.description:
Run a lionagi engine of a specific kind.

Available kinds: coding, hypothesis, planning, research, review

Progress events are written to stderr as human-readable lines.
The final result is written as JSON to stdout.

schema.title: handshake
schema.description: The version a machine consumer negotiates against at registration. Add `machine` for the contract envelope on stdout.

source.description: Which harness wrote the config being imported: 'claude' for Claude Code's settings.json shape, 'codex' for the Codex hooks.json shape.

path.description: Config file to read. Defaults to .claude/settings.json or .codex/hooks.json under the project directory, matching the source given.

cwd.description: Project whose .lionagi/settings.yaml receives the imported hooks, and where the default config path is looked up (defaults to the current directory).
Project whose imported hook commands are listed and approved (defaults to the current directory).

yes.description: Record trust without an interactive confirmation prompt.

invocation_id.description: The id printed by `li invoke start`. An invocation never closed stays 'running' forever.

status.description: How the work ended, which also fixes the reason stored with it: 'completed' for success, 'failed' for an exception, 'timed_out' for a deadline, 'aborted' for a user interrupt, 'cancelled' for a system cancellation. Later listings and dashboards filter on this, so leaving the default on work that did not succeed records it as a success.

metadata.description: JSON merged key-by-key into the invocation's existing metadata, so anything written during the run survives unless this overwrites that key.

skill.description: Show only invocations of this skill name, matched exactly.

status.description: Show only invocations in this status: running, completed, failed, timed_out, aborted or cancelled.

limit.description: Maximum rows to print, newest first (default 20).

skill.description: Name of the orchestration being recorded, e.g. 'show', 'codex-pr-review' or 'reprompt'. Every session spawned under this id groups by it.

plugin.description: Marketplace plugin packaging that skill, when the skill came from one.

prompt.description: The request that triggered this work, stored as free text for later reading.

metadata.description: Skill-specific JSON to attach (e.g. show plan, review rounds). Stored verbatim; rendered as-is on the invocation detail page.

schema.title: kill

id.description: Entity id to kill: run_id / session_id / invocation_id / play_id / show_id. Accepts a full UUID, or an id prefix (resolved to the first matching row).

reason.description: Optional human-readable reason recorded in status_transitions.

recursive.description: Also kill direct child entities (e.g. invocations spawned by a session). Has no effect on a play kill, which already reaps whatever worker chain the row records, or on a show kill, which cannot reach one -- kill the session ids directly to stop a show's workers.

all_stale.description: Sweep stale sessions and invocations with dead PIDs older than `threshold`. A play older than `threshold` whose recorded worker session has gone terminal is marked 'blocked'; a play that records no worker session is left running, because age alone cannot tell it apart from one still working. A show is marked 'aborted' only once it is older than `threshold` and ALL of its plays are terminal.

threshold.description: Stale threshold in seconds (default 3600 = 1h). Only entities started more than this many seconds ago are swept.

dry_run.description: Print what would be killed/cancelled without making any changes.

grace.description: Seconds to wait after SIGTERM before escalating to SIGKILL (default 5).

schema.description:
Kill a running lionagi entity by id, or sweep all stale running entities whose underlying OS process is dead.

The entity's status is set to 'cancelled' (sessions/invocations), 'blocked' (plays), or 'aborted' (shows) with reason tracking per ADR-0028.

Recursion boundary: `recursive` kills a session's or invocation's direct children, which are the PID-bearing workers. A PLAY kill reaches the play's worker chain only when the row records the session it started; a play created by a live run does not, so that kill marks the row terminal and exits non-zero to say no worker was stopped. A SHOW kill only marks the show row terminal. To stop work either one cannot reach, kill the session ids directly; `all_stale` marks a play 'blocked' only when the row records a worker session that has gone terminal, and leaves an unlinked play running.

Examples:
  li kill abc123                        # kill by id prefix
  li kill <session-id>                  # stop a worker process
  li kill abc123 --reason 'stuck'
  li kill abc123 --recursive            # kill + direct children
  li kill --all-stale                   # sweep dead-PID rows
  li kill --all-stale --threshold 3600  # only rows older than 1h
  li kill --all-stale --dry-run

schema.title: lifecycle

run_id.description: The run id to report on.

schema.description: Read-only: what the lifecycle store records about one run id — whether a session was ever recorded for it, whether every one of them has ended, and with what outcome. A run stopped by `li kill` reads as cancelled here. Add `machine` for the contract envelope on stdout.

schema.title: mcp

action.description: What to do: 'serve' (the default and only value) runs the server on stdin/stdout until the client disconnects.

schema.description: Serve the lionagi MCP server over stdio. It advertises one tool, request(ops=[{op, args}], help?), with every operation behind it as a namespaced verb: agent.submit, flow.submit, fanout.submit and play.submit start detached background runs, job.status, job.output, job.list, job.wait and job.kill follow them. Call request(help=true) for the verb catalog and request(help="<verb>") for one verb's parameters, generated from this CLI's own parsers. Requires the 'mcp' extra: pip install 'lionagi[mcp]'.

schema.title: monitor

id.description: Run, session, play or show to open in the detail view — full id, or an unambiguous prefix. Omit it for the table of everything in flight.

watch.description: Redraw the view every `refresh` seconds until interrupted, instead of printing one snapshot and exiting.

refresh.description: Seconds between redraws under `watch` (default 2). Ignored without it.

since.description: Only show entities updated within this time window. Format: 30m, 1h, 2d (minutes/hours/days). Default: all running.

entity_type.description: Narrow the table to one kind of entity: session, invocation, show or play.

project.description: Filter sessions and plays to one project name, matched exactly — the same name the table's project column shows.

run_ids.description: Wait for one or more schedule_run IDs to reach a terminal state, then exit (scripting primitive; see `li monitor run --help` for the positional form). Follows scheduler on_success/on_fail chain children by default (see `chain`). Ignores id/`watch` / `since` / `entity_type` / `project`.

interval.description: Seconds between state.db polls in `run_ids` mode (default 3). Independent of `refresh`, which paces the table redraw.

follow.description: With `run_ids`: keep discovering schedule_runs created after the initial set drains, instead of exiting once it is empty. Never ends on its own — pair with `max_wait`.

chain.description: With `run_ids`: watch only the literal id(s) given, instead of following scheduler on_success/on_fail chain children by default.

max_wait.description: With `run_ids`: give up waiting after this many seconds and exit EXIT_RUNNING for whatever is still pending, instead of blocking forever on a stuck session or run. Default: 900s. Pass 0 for unlimited.

schema.description: Show all running entities (sessions, invocations, shows, plays) in a compact table, or drill into one entity by ID. Use `watch` for live refresh.

schema.title: orchestrate ctl msg

id.description: Running flow, playbook run, or agent leg to message, by session, invocation, play, or run id (full, or an unambiguous prefix).

text.description: Message merged into the flow's workspace context. Ops already started will not see it; every op that has not started yet will.

schema.description: Queues a message control row. A flow or playbook run's control poller deep-merges it into the workspace context, visible to any op not yet started (context mode only; --as-op is not supported by this command yet). A running `li agent` leg instead drains it at its next turn boundary, landing as a warm continuation turn rather than a context merge — check `li o ctl status` for which happened.

schema.title: orchestrate ctl pause

id.description: Running flow to pause, by session, invocation, play, or run id (full, or an unambiguous prefix). The pause lands at the next op boundary, not mid-op.

schema.description: Queues a pause control row; the target flow's control poller applies it at the next op boundary (idempotent — safe to queue more than once).

schema.title: orchestrate ctl resolve

control_id.description: The control id shown by `li o ctl status` (full, no prefix matching).

outcome.description: What you established actually happened: 'applied' if the message reached the run, 'abandoned' if it did not and will not.

actor.description: Who resolved it, recorded beside the claim. Defaults to the OS account running the command; pass this when that is not the person who found out.

schema.description: A `msg` control is delivered at most once, so a consumer claims it before attempting the delivery. If that consumer dies in between, nothing left behind can say whether the message reached the model, and the row is deliberately left standing rather than guessed at. `li o ctl status` shows who claimed it and when. Use this once you have found out which it was; the claim is preserved in the record.

schema.title: orchestrate ctl resume

id.description: Paused flow to release, by session, invocation, play, or run id (full, or an unambiguous prefix).

schema.description: Queues a resume control row, releasing a pending pause gate.

schema.title: orchestrate ctl status

id.description: Session, invocation, play, or run id to report on — full, or an unambiguous prefix. Required here: this command has no 'latest run' default.

as_json.description: Print one JSON object with stable keys instead of the human table, for scripting.

schema.description: Generic id-addressed status lookup — no agent/play kind scoping, so <id> is required (no 'latest run' default). Prefer `li agent status` / `li play status` when the kind is known.

schema.title: orchestrate fanout

query.description: Orchestrator model spec (provider/model-effort) followed by the task prompt. Model is also used as the default worker model unless `workers` is set; omit it when `agent` provides one. A single positional is treated as the prompt.

agent.description: Load orchestrator profile by name. Resolves .lionagi/agents/<NAME>/<NAME>.md first, then .lionagi/agents/<NAME>.md. Profile provides system prompt, default model, effort, yolo. CLI flags and positional model override profile settings.

num_workers.description: Maximum assignments the orchestrator generates (default 3). It may generate fewer if the task does not divide that far, and `workers` specs beyond this cap go unused.

workers.description: Comma-separated worker model specs, assigned round-robin (each may carry an effort suffix). This is how one fanout mixes cheap and expensive models across workers.

pack.description: Path to a YAML routing pack. Provides per-role model/effort when `workers` is absent. `workers` overrides pack routing.

max_concurrent.description: Cap on workers running at the same time. 0, the default, runs them all at once — lower it to stay under a provider's rate limit.

with_synthesis.description: Run a final pass merging the workers' results into one answer. Bare flag uses the orchestrator model; with an argument, that model instead.

synthesis_prompt.description: What the merged answer should be — a ranked list, a decision, a single patch. Implies synthesis.

output.description: Result format: 'text' (default) for reading, 'json' for a machine-readable run.

save.description: Directory to write each worker's output and the run's artifacts into. Without it they land in the run's own artifacts directory.

team_mode.description: Create a persistent team for this fanout. Workers get team context and results are posted as team messages. Bare flag uses 'fanout' as team name; with arg uses that name.

mcp_config.description: Read this MCP config and hand its servers to every worker this run builds. By default the nearest .mcp.json at or above the directory this command was run in is used, so the workers' tools come from the submission rather than from `cwd`. The file is read once, at startup.

no_mcp_config.description: Hand the workers no MCP servers, and say so deliberately instead of arriving there by an empty search.

yolo.description: Auto-approve the agent's tool calls, so an unattended run is never left waiting.

bypass.description: Bypass all codex approvals and sandbox (for cloud/codespace environments).

fast.description: Route codex requests through OpenAI's priority service tier (lower latency; requires account eligibility). Does not change model or reasoning effort.

verbose.description: Stream the agent's output as it is produced instead of printing only the final result, and silence the progress lines that would interleave with it.

theme.description: Pick the colour scheme printed output is tuned for: 'light' or 'dark' terminal.

effort.description: Override effort (overrides spec suffix). claude: low|medium|high|xhigh|max. codex: none|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max|ultra (max/ultra clamp per model support). gemini-code/gemini-cli: folded into --model as Low|Medium|High (Gemini 3.1 Pro has no Medium).

cwd.description: Directory the agent's process runs in — the repo or worktree it acts on. Defaults to the current directory.

timeout.description: Hard wall-clock timeout in seconds. When set, a [DEADLINE] preamble is injected into the agent's prompt so the agent knows its time budget and can pace reasoning accordingly.

invocation.description: Parent invocation id (from `li invoke start`). Groups this session under a skill orchestration record. Optional.

project.description: Explicit project name for this session. Overrides auto-detection from .lionagi/config.toml or git remote.

resume_on_timeout.description: Deprecated and ignored on this command: it is accepted so existing invocations keep working, but nothing here reads it and it will be removed in a future release. Only `li agent` implements it.

notify.description: Shell command template run once this run reaches its terminal status. Overrides .lionagi/settings.yaml notify.on_terminal. Substitutes {payload} (full JSON), {status}, {invocation_id}.

schema.description: Orchestrator decomposes task into N agent requests, fans out to workers, optionally synthesizes. Effort can be embedded in model spec: claude/opus-4-7-high. Flags may appear anywhere relative to the positionals.

schema.title: orchestrate flow

query.description: Orchestrator model spec followed by the task prompt. Model is optional when `agent` provides one; a single positional is treated as the prompt. The prompt itself may instead come from `file` or `playbook`.

file.description: Load flow spec from YAML or JSON file. File values serve as defaults; CLI flags override them. Prompt can come from the file (prompt: key) or as a positional argument.

playbook.description: Load playbook from ~/.lionagi/playbooks/<NAME>.playbook.yaml. Playbooks may declare args: schema, artifacts: contracts, or argument-hint: placeholders for prompt template values.

agent.description: Load orchestrator profile by name — resolves .lionagi/agents/<NAME>/<NAME>.md first, then .lionagi/agents/<NAME>.md.

with_synthesis.description: Run a final pass merging the DAG's results into one answer. Bare flag uses the orchestrator model; with an argument, that model instead.

max_concurrent.description: Cap on agents running at the same time within one phase. 0, the default, runs the whole phase at once — lower it to stay under a provider's rate limit.

output.description: Result format: 'text' (default) for reading, 'json' for a machine-readable run.

save.description: Directory to write each agent's output and the run's artifacts into. Required by `background`, which has nowhere else to report.

team_mode.description: Create a FRESH team for this flow (new UUID every invocation). Bare flag uses 'flow' as the name.

team_attach.description: Attach to a team by NAME — upsert semantics: load existing team if found (preserving message history), else create fresh. Mutually exclusive with `team_mode`.

team_max_rounds.description: In team mode (reactive), how many extra wakeup rounds the coordinator may run after all currently-running workers signal done, to deliver unread teammate messages before the run wraps up (default: 2).

dry_run.description: Plan the DAG but don't execute. Shows agents, deps, and model resolution.

show_graph.description: Render DAG as matplotlib visualization. With `save`, saves PNG to save dir.

background.description: Run flow in background. Requires `save`. Check output in save dir.

bare.description: Ignore agent profiles — all workers use the CLI model spec. Roles define behavioral focus only, no profile system prompts.

workers.description: Comma-separated worker model specs (assignment i uses pool[i % len]). Overrides the per-role model while KEEPING each role's profile/system prompt — unlike `bare`, which also drops profiles. Enables mixed-model flows (cheap roles + expensive roles).

pack.description: Path to a YAML routing pack. Provides per-role model/effort when `workers` is absent. `workers` overrides pack routing.

max_ops.description: Cap total ops (nodes in the planned DAG). 0 = no shared ceiling; reactive spawns are capped at 20. `--max-agents` is a deprecated alias — prefer `--max-ops`.

reactive.description: Who may grow the live DAG by emitting a SpawnRequest: 'all' (default — every worker), 'off' (flat batch DAG, no spawning), or a comma-separated list of roles (e.g. 'critic,evaluator') that alone may spawn. Caps still apply via `max_ops`.

resume.description: Resume a checkpointed flow from a prior process (by run id, or any session/invocation/play id backed by one). Replays the persisted plan verbatim — no planner call, no other flow flags read (model/prompt/playbook/etc. all come from the checkpoint). Distinct from `li o ctl resume`, which un-pauses a still-running session.

retry_failed.description: With `resume`: run the ops the checkpoint recorded as failed again, instead of refusing. Their reactive children from the superseded attempt are dropped so the re-run decides its own. Without this flag a checkpoint holding any failed op refuses loudly, naming them, because replaying one as terminal skips it and everything downstream. Re-running re-executes whatever side effects the first attempt already had.

allow_degraded_context.description: With `resume`: proceed even when a pending op declared inherit_context — it runs against an empty branch instead of its predecessor's conversation history, which resume does not restore. Without this flag such ops refuse loudly, naming them.

mcp_config.description: Read this MCP config and hand its servers to every worker this run builds. By default the nearest .mcp.json at or above the directory this command was run in is used, so the workers' tools come from the submission rather than from `cwd`. The file is read once, at startup.

invocation.description: Parent invocation id (from `li invoke start`). Groups this session under a skill orchestration record. Optional.

schema.description: Orchestrator analyzes the task, composes a DAG of agents with dependency edges, and executes with automatic parallelism where dependencies allow. Flags may appear anywhere relative to the positionals.
schema.x-playbook-arguments: This command accepts arguments declared by the playbook named in 'playbook'. Ask for this schema again with that playbook named to see them.

schema.title: plugin disable

name.description: Plugin to leave installed and trusted but inert, as named by `li plugin list`. Re-enable it with `li plugin enable`.

schema.description: A settings flag, not a file mutation — the bundle stays pristine.

name.description: Plugin to load again, as named by `li plugin list`. It must already be trusted.
Plugin to describe — its manifest `name:`, as listed by `li plugin list`.

schema.title: plugin list

schema.title: schedule create

name.description: Unique name identifying this schedule. Reused as the display label in listings; a name already in use is rejected rather than overwritten.

trigger_type.description: Trigger type (default: cron). 'github' is an alias for 'github_poll'.

cron.description: Cron expression, e.g. "0 * * * *". Required when `trigger_type` is cron, which is the default; ignored for other trigger types.

interval.description: Seconds between fires. Required when `trigger_type` is interval; ignored for other trigger types.

github_repo.description: GitHub repository to poll (required for `trigger_type` github/github_poll).

github_filter.description: JSON object filtering which PRs fire the trigger, e.g. '{"state": "open", "base": "main"}'.

threshold_config.description: Metric threshold alert config as a JSON object: {"metric": "failed_sessions|total_cost_usd|p95_latency_ms|github_poll_healthy_age_minutes|github_poll_consecutive_401", "op": "gt|gte", "value": N, "window_minutes": N}. When set, this schedule's own cron/interval cadence only evaluates the metric on each tick and fires the action only when the threshold is breached (cooldown = window_minutes). Full validation happens server-side, e.g. '{"metric": "failed_sessions", "op": "gt", "value": 5, "window_minutes": 60}'.

poll_interval.description: How often to poll GitHub, in seconds (github_poll only).

action_kind.description: Stored action kind or accepted alias (default: agent).

prompt.description: Instruction the scheduled agent runs at each fire. Required when `action_kind` is agent, which is the default. A profile named by `agent` supplies the model and settings, never this instruction, so a schedule created without it fires and fails.

agent.description: Agent profile to run, resolved the same way `li agent --agent` resolves it. Supplies the system prompt, model and effort the fire runs with.

flow_yaml.description: Path to a YAML flow spec file (for action-kind=flow_yaml).

action_command.description: Executable name to spawn directly, bypassing `li` (for action-kind=command). Must be a bare name (no path separators) and be a member of LIONAGI_SCHEDULER_COMMAND_ALLOWLIST; refused loudly at create time and re-checked at fire time.

action_command_args.description: action-kind=command argv, as a JSON array of {{var}} templates rendered from trigger_context at fire time, e.g. '["review-pr", "--pr", "{{pr_number}}"]'.

project.description: Project this schedule's runs are recorded under. Defaults to the project detected from the execution root.

cwd.description: Explicit execution root for this schedule's spawned process (must be an existing directory). Persisted at creation time so the schedule's spawn cwd never depends on where the Studio daemon is running from (default: `project`'s registered path, or this CLI's own working directory).

max_runs.description: Auto-disable this schedule once N total runs have fired (default: unlimited). Chained on_success/on_fail fires do not count toward N. Mutually exclusive with `once`.

once.description: Sugar for `max_runs` 1 — fire once, then auto-disable.

max_cost_usd.description: Auto-disable this schedule once its cumulative session spend reaches USD (default: unlimited). Pre-fire cumulative gate: an in-flight run is not interrupted, so the schedule may overshoot by up to one run's cost before the next fire is refused.

max_tokens.description: Auto-disable this schedule once its cumulative session token usage (input+output) reaches N (default: unlimited). Same pre-fire cumulative semantics as `max_cost_usd`.

on_success.description: Chain action to fire when this run exits 0, as a JSON object (allowed keys: kind/action_kind, model, prompt, agent, playbook, on_success, on_fail). WARNING — shallow merge: the chain child is built as {**this_schedule, **on_success}, so any key you omit is INHERITED from this schedule, including on_success/on_fail themselves. A 2-level chain must set the inner level's own "on_success": null explicitly, or the chain keeps re-firing at each depth (capped, but rarely what you want). Example value: {"prompt": "notify done", "on_success": null}

on_fail.description: Chain action to fire when this run exits non-zero, as a JSON object (same allowed keys and shallow-merge caveat as `on_success` — see above). Example value: {"prompt": "alert on-call", "on_fail": null}

schema.title: state checkpoint

mode.description: How hard to push the WAL back into the database. TRUNCATE (default) frees the WAL file outright but needs no active readers; PASSIVE, FULL and RESTART give up completeness to avoid blocking. No run data is lost in any mode.

schema.description: Run PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE|PASSIVE|RESTART|FULL). Default is TRUNCATE — most aggressive, frees the WAL file if no readers are active.

schema.title: state doctor

dry_run.description: Print what WOULD be swept, but don't update rows.

schema.description: A SIGKILL or unclean exit between session-open and teardown leaves the session row at status='running' forever. This command resets such rows (older than `stale_hours`, default 24) to `new_status` (default 'aborted'). Conservative: a session is swept only if its started_at is older than the threshold AND its recorded process is not running, so an actively-running CLI process is left alone even when the session it resumed started long ago. Use `dry_run` first.

schema.title: state import
schema.description: Scan ~/.lionagi/runs/ for run directories with run.json manifests and load their sessions, branches, and messages into state.db. Already-imported sessions are skipped (idempotent).

schema.title: state import-teams
schema.description: Scan ~/.lionagi/teams/*.json and INSERT each team + its messages into the `teams` and `team_messages` tables. Idempotent: existing rows (matched by team id) are left alone. Run once after upgrading; the runtime can keep using JSON until the dual-write path ships.

schema.title: state ls

status.description: Show only sessions in this status: running, completed, failed or aborted. Omit to list every status.

schema.description: Print a table of sessions stored in state.db.

schema.title: state null-content

older_than.description: Reclaim bodies older than N days. Required and deliberately has no default: there is no age that is safe to assume for an irreversible operation.

role.description: Limit to messages with this role; repeatable. Omitted means every role. Check `li state stats` first — the roles are not evenly sized, and one of them usually holds most of the bytes.

dry_run.description: Perform the reclaim and roll it back, reporting what it measured.

schema.description:
Reclaim the space held by message bodies older than `older_than` days, keeping every row, id, role, timestamp and progression reference. THIS IS WHERE THE BYTES ARE, and prune cannot reach them: prune selects SESSIONS, and a message any surviving progression still names is kept whatever its age. A store can therefore be almost entirely message content, have every message inside a keep-window, and give a prune nothing to delete.

A reclaimed body is not emptied. It is replaced with a marker recording that a body was there and how large it was, so it stays distinguishable from a turn that genuinely produced nothing. Reclaiming is not reversible: the text is gone.

The file does not shrink. Freed pages return to the database's own free list and the bytes on disk stay where they are until `li state vacuum` rebuilds the file.

`dry_run` is not a read. It performs the update and rolls it back, so its numbers measure the operation instead of estimating it, and it takes the same write lock for the same duration.

schema.title: state prune

keep_days.description: Keep sessions updated within the last N days (default 30).

keep_n.description: Always keep the N most recent sessions (default 100).

dry_run.description: Print what WOULD be deleted, but don't actually delete.

schema.description:
Delete sessions older than `keep_days` (default 30), keeping the most recent `keep_n` (default 100). Foreign key cascades drop branches; messages are dropped if no other session references them via progression. Use `dry_run` to preview.

SESSIONS ARE THE AXIS, AND MESSAGES HOLD THE BYTES. A message a surviving progression still names is kept whatever its age, so a run can delete thousands of sessions and free no message rows. Read the message counts, not the session count, to judge whether this reclaimed space; `li state stats` shows both distributions.

`dry_run` is not a read. It runs the real deletes and rolls the transaction back, which is what makes its counts exact rather than estimated, and which means it takes the same write lock for the same duration as the real thing.

schema.title: state stats
schema.description: Report state.db + state.db-wal sizes, per-table row counts, messages broken down by role and by age, session status distribution, and SQLite PRAGMAs (journal_mode, wal_autocheckpoint, busy_timeout). Use to spot growth and lock contention, and to check before pruning whether the keep-window can reach anything at all.

schema.title: state vacuum
schema.description: Run VACUUM — rebuilds the entire DB file, reclaiming pages freed by previous deletes. Holds an exclusive lock for the duration. Run after `li state prune`.

schema.title: stats runs

since.description: Only include runs updated within this window. Format: 30m, 1h, 7d. Default: 7d.

group_by.description: Comma-separated group keys from {project, kind, agent, model, status}. Default: project,kind.

json.description: Emit a JSON array of row objects instead of an aligned table.

schema.description: Aggregate sessions rows updated within `since` into run_count, completed, and failed counts per group. Read-only: no writes, no schema changes, no PRAGMA mutations.
